source.title: Sparse Coding, for Mechanistic Interpretability and Activation Engineering

record.tranche_reason: The post measures token activations for native language-model neurons using top-token inspection, a different measurement from the original vision-model examples.
record.gate_note: The post lists top tokens for ten native Llama-2 7B neurons, but does not define or score token relatedness or estimate how common mixed responses are. Its extensive sparse-autoencoder feature lists concern learned autoencoder units, not native MLP neurons; they are not rows for these claim versions. Alternative interpretability methods and sparsity values are discussed, but no comparative outcome on native-neuron polysemanticity is reported.
record.test_reason: The post uses superposition as motivation for training sparse autoencoders and reports how interpretable the autoencoder features look. Its only native-unit result is a ten-unit Llama-2 7B top-token baseline. That baseline is illustrative, with no relatedness criterion or prevalence estimate. The units appear to be residual-stream basis dimensions, not MLP neurons, so it does not measure what V2 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author argues that superposition makes native activation directions polysemantic. He reports that L1-sparse autoencoder directions on Pythia-70M and Llama-2 7B look semantically meaningful under top-token inspection, unlike a native-unit baseline. Early layers look most interpretable and later layers more garbled. He cautions that the method is naive and the code may have bugs.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains L1-sparse autoencoders on model-layer activations and inspects their learned directions with top-token lists; it also gives a top-token baseline for native neurons. It does not reproduce the original vision-model neuron analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: The first ten (unsorted, indices 0–9) layer-13 basis units of Llama-2 7B each have top input tokens with no evident shared theme, such as 'bus, Sund, marriage, breakfast'. Sparse-autoencoder directions on the same layer look more coherent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream basis dimensions of transformer LMs look polysemantic under top-token inspection, while sparse-autoencoder directions look more monosemantic.

record.problems: The native-neuron baseline is ten illustrated neurons from one layer of one model, with no stated sampling method. The top-token method does not establish whether the tokens are unrelated or how prevalent such responses are. The author calls the method naive and notes that the code may contain bugs; no controls or uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Sparse-autoencoder feature token lists and sparsity settings are omitted because they describe learned autoencoder units rather than native neurons, and do not measure the claim versions' native-neuron outcomes.

untested.parts: No MLP-neuron share is measured, and there is no layer comparison of native neurons.
Superposition is argued theoretically and assumed; capacity pressure is not tested as a cause.
No comparison of architecture, activation function or regularization for native neurons.
Top-token inspection is called naive, but measurements are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' is not justified. The baseline is an unquantified illustration, and the units are likely residual-stream dimensions rather than MLP neurons. The polysemanticity claim is assumed as motivation, not tested. The SAE feature lists are correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Vision classifiers and InceptionV1 are not tested.
The post shows ten neurons from one Llama-2 7B layer, not a representative share of MLP neurons or a layer-by-layer comparison. It does not operationalize whether the tokens are unrelated.
The post gives a theoretical superposition argument and trains overcomplete autoencoders, but does not test whether capacity pressure causes native-neuron polysemanticity.
Initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes without capacity pressure are not tested.
The post does not compare architectures or activation functions, measure native-neuron polysemanticity across them, or report the performance cost of reducing it.
The post does not use improved tools to establish whether canonical mixed native neurons detect one shared feature.
It notes that top-token inspection is naive and mentions other possible tools, but does not compare measurements or activation ranges.

rows.subject: Llama-2 7B
rows.operation_detail: Top-input-token inspection of native model neurons
rows.measure: Top input tokens for each illustrated neuron
rows.value: The post lists these token groups for neurons 0–9: Rafael/animation/ovo/beneath/commun/Cross; Hero/emor/action/Indones/expedition/immer; bus/Sund/top/marriage/ander/breakfast; predict/Ald/phase/overcome/rin/Joy; related/lazy/round/Nev/UI/atmosphere; trans/gu/isted/portal/tiny/laimed; ija/Chief/measures/valuable/space/testing; ond/lazy/Virgin/tes/conquer/uniform; Valley/ctions/round/measures/facilities/variable; ways/definitely/isation/elements/enta/expl.
rows.note: One row records the ten illustrated neurons as a group; the post supplies token lists but no criterion for judging whether their meanings are unrelated or a prevalence estimate.
rows.check: The 'neurons' are probably layer-13 residual-stream basis dimensions, not MLP neurons. The Pythia autoencoders are described as trained on residual streams, and the Llama autoencoder widths (~41k) match about 10x the 4096-dimensional residual width. V2 names MLP neurons. The row is also an illustrative baseline for the author's method, not a measure of how common the behaviour is, and has no criterion for 'unrelated'. The subject should state 'residual-stream dimensions (probable)'.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
